title: Field & Furrow
summary: A farmer's book, plain and proven. Good for any honest field. — T. Ashby

pages.text: Walk the field at first light {~with the bag at your belt~}; scatter {~a pinch at every tenth pace~}. The grain fills out by harvest.
Set the iron in the first furrow {~and the plough remembers it~}. Every furrow after {~runs true~}.
For orchards. Bury the wire {~at the root~} and {~the tree remembers to drink~} through a dry summer.
{~Spoken over~} a neighbour's grain, it brings the red rust {~in a single night~}. {~Useful against weed-wheat that will not be pulled~}, and {~never on your own land~}.
pages.authorNote: Outlier. Legible: "a neighbour's grain, it brings the red rust". Hennie's temptation.

pages.text: Call a little rain onto your own ground {~and no one else's~}. Ask {~before noon~}.
